pass_b_english: The third offering he made to him was this: only the wise man is truly rich and renowned, because within him lies the possession of many things and the offspring of wisdom. If one sows these into the spirit, they reap life. It seems he speaks of his own wealth when he says: You need no expense, no innovation, for your love toward me; it is enough to love only, and you will be loved in return. Moreover, what is wonderful—that righteousness resides in wealth—is also true with me, and this, along with all other things, is good. The substance that is God’s wisdom existed begotten before the ages and eternal before creation; but when it entered into relation with the generated, it became the beginning of God’s ways, the creative and providential. Thus the beginning is a spouse to the creations of which it is the beginning—that is, the relation toward the generated. But wisdom is eternal, substantially existing before the ages with God. Impiety is sin against God; and impious, too, is anyone who stores up punishment for his own soul, prepared for the impious. Consequently, loving death belongs to those who hate wisdom, if wisdom is life. Taking hold of wisdom here doubly: I mean that which comes from the Holy Spirit, given in words and writing to the godly-minded, through which the knowledge of God was made known to the world. Likewise, the hypostatic Son and Word of God, who brought all things from non-being into being by his wisdom. The sacrifices he refers to are those prophets who were sealed and slaughtered by the praise of Christ, because they sifted them with the vessel of knowledge—the sweet understanding of him for the intelligent—saying: Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul; for he himself slaughtered them and slays them, because he himself urges those who believe in him for himself, as he himself dies for you. If Paul the apostle is a slave of Christ, and Christ is wisdom, then Paul is a slave of wisdom. Likewise, we will gather the word of the remaining apostles and prophets, having shown themselves slaves of his wisdom. We ought not to reprove sinners, but to remind them of divine fear. Whoever turns them away from evil, or those who are evil returning from sin and wishing to come to repentance—be patient with evil ones blinding them, and do not rebuke for a single fault, lest they come to hatred from beginnings. But when they become wise and strengthened, then rebuke. And Christ did not rebuke his disciples while they were young, because they were not the old ascetics ready for new wine. Or he calls foolish the senseless and stupid, or those entirely alien from divine teaching—whom we ought not to rebuke, but to admonish, to teach, and to instruct. choices.choice: rich: Primary sense of wealth in context of wisdom’s inner abundance; matches 'possession of many things'.
righteousness: Fits parallel structure with wisdom’s attributes; theological term for right standing before God.
possession: Concrete noun for what wisdom contains; better than 'property' for inner, spiritual assets.
